# __R Tutorial: T-test__
```{r message=F, warning=F}
library(tidyverse)
library(lessR)
library(readxl)
library(BSDA)
```
```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = "C:/Users/egrio/OneDrive/Escritorio/ants_r/Edwin-s-R-Introduction-Class/rtutorials/butterflies") 
```

```{r}
butterflies <- read_excel("butterflies_pesticides.xlsx")
head(butterflies)
```
__Q1. Normality test__
```{r}
shapiro.test(butterflies$Wing_Length[butterflies$Group=="group1"])
shapiro.test(butterflies$Wing_Length[butterflies$Group=="group2"])

# Wing length did not significantly deviate from a normal distribution in either the control group (W = 0.958, p = 0.146) or the pesticide-treated group (W = 0.978, p = 0.625), indicating that the normality assumption was met.
```
__Q2. Equality of variances test__
```{r}
var.test(Wing_Length~Group, butterflies)

# Homogeneity of variances was assessed using an F-test. The test indicated that variances differed significantly between the control and pesticide-treated groups, F = 0.40274, df = 39, p = 0.005512. Therefore, the assumption of equal variances was violated, and Welch's t-test was used for subsequent analyses.
```
__Q3. Statistical test__
```{r}
t.test(Wing_Length~Group,
       butterflies,
       var.equal=F)

# Welch's t-test indicated a significant difference in wing length between pesticide-treated and untreated butterflies, t = 3.98, p = 0.00017. Butterflies in the control group exhibited a greater mean wing length than butterflies exposed to pesticides during larval development.
```
__Q4. ggplot__
```{r}
ggplot(butterflies,
       aes(x=Group,
           y=Wing_Length,
           fill = Group)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Wing Length by Group",
       x="Treatment Group",
       y="Wing Length")
```


__Q5. Summary paragraph__
```{r}
# The objective of this study was to determine whether pesticide exposure during the larval stage affects butterfly wing length. Normality was assessed using Shapiro-Wilk tests, and both the control group (W = 0.95826, p = 0.146) and pesticide-treated group (W = 0.97825, p = 0.6247) met the assumption of normality. An F-test showed unequal variances between groups, F = 0.40274, df = 39, p = 0.005512; therefore, Welch's two-sample t-test was performed. Results revealed a significant difference in wing length between groups, t = 3.9832, df = 66.029, p = 0.0001721. Butterflies exposed to pesticides had a lower mean wing length than untreated butterflies. Because the p-value was less than 0.05, the null hypothesis was rejected. These findings suggest that pesticide exposure during larval development negatively impacts butterfly growth, resulting in smaller adult wing lengths.  
```
